invariants.title: Money is integer minor units, signed; every source and transaction carries a currency; sums are per currency and never cross.
Every transaction traces to a source: source id, row index, and the raw line as read.

A statement is accepted whole or not at all: the rows must reconcile to the printed opening and closing balance, and to the printed row count when the statement prints one, or the batch is refused with the gap named.
The same source hash is refused a second time; rows already present are skipped and listed, never silently merged or duplicated.
Nothing is invented: category, vendor and status are empty or unreviewed until an act with a reason sets them.
A subscription is declared, then confirmed by the record: a period with no matching charge is missed, two make it lapsed; a charge is never assumed.
A receipt matches at most one transaction and vice versa; matching is a reasoned act, refused when the total or date does not fit unless overridden with a reason.
Every write is a logged act with an actor; refusals are logged too.
Files never live here: a source or a receipt is its hash, its metadata and what was read.
A standing rule suggests and never books: matching rows stay unreviewed with the suggestion until a reasoned review confirms them; ending a rule removes its suggestions and changes no reviewed row.

A bill is a record, never a payment: only a person approves paying it, a payment is recorded after it happened and by an agent only for an approved bill, a linked statement row must match it, and the same bill is refused twice.
Every statement belongs to one account; an account's statements chain, and a gap, an overlap or an opening that is not the last closing is named, never smoothed.
A balance is what a statement printed or a value a person stated, each with its date and source; nothing is extrapolated or estimated.
Net worth is per currency: what is held less what is owed, each line showing as of when; figures older than 45 days are named.
A move between two of the person's accounts is one transfer: its two sides paired, exactly opposite, counted once, never as spending or income.
Pairing is a reasoned act on rows not already booked otherwise; suggestions never pair; unpairing puts both rows back as they were.
A transfer naming one of the person's accounts with no other side is listed, saying whether that account's statement should already show it.
A card statement's printed facts (minimum payment, due date, credit limit, rate) are kept as printed; changing them is a correction with a reason.
A card payment is due from the statement's facts and met by payments seen into the card by the due date; a missed one is named, never assumed paid.
A refund is tied to the purchase it reverses, never more than is left of it; it takes back spending in the purchase's category and is not income.
Interest and fees are what rows reviewed as fees say, per card and year; nothing is estimated from the rate.
